page: Microsoft Azure L48as_v3 is a storage-optimized virtual machine driven by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at up to 3.525 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance supplies 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The memory footprint comprises 384.0 GB of RAM, equating to an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of 12,035 GB of integrated NVMe SSD capacity, providing substantial direct-attached solid-state storage. No dedicated GPUs are included with this server configuration.

Performance benchmarks show strong multi-threaded capabilities alongside capable single-core execution. The instance recorded 64,762.99 on the stress-ng multi-core test and a Geekbench multi-core score of 16,236.0, both placing in the top 25%. Hardware cryptographic acceleration contributes to a PassMark CPU encryption score of 51,422.08, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 251.2 GB/sec. Memory subsystem testing reflects 110.18 GB/sec read bandwidth and 60.68 GB/sec write bandwidth on large un-cached blocks, landing in the middle 50% band.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L48as_v3 targets workloads that need dense local NVMe storage coupled with high memory capacity without the necessity of external storage attachments. The primary hardware tradeoff is the reliance on standard AVX rather than AVX-512 extensions, alongside an absence of dedicated GPUs, which bounds certain machine learning and specialized vector tasks. Given its storage density, 384.0 GB RAM, and solid parallel processing, the instance is well suited for distributed NoSQL databases, transactional engines, data warehousing, large-scale caching systems, and heavy ETL pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure L48as_v3 is a storage-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz on x86_64 architecture. It provides 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores, 384.0 GB of system memory (8.0 GB per vCPU), and 12,035 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The platform omits discrete GPUs, relying on strong CPU multi-threading that placed it in the top 25% for PassMark CPU (51,293.97) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (251.2 GB/sec). Memory bandwidth delivers 110.18 GB/sec for large un-cached reads, while Redis throughput reaches 47.67 million operations per second. Balancing high memory capacity with massive local NVMe disk space, the L48as_v3 is designed for I/O-intensive workloads including transactional databases, NoSQL clusters, data warehousing, and distributed data processing frameworks.
